contents.content: Write an e-mail requesting an informational interview.
Instructions: Complete the following steps. Fill in the Self Assessment.

images.text:
From: k.lenard@mail.com
To: danielle_wilkinson@WXBJ.com
Subject: Request for Informational Interview – Harvard Alumni

Dear Ms. Wilkinson,
I was given your contact information by my mother. She mentioned that you received your Bachelor of Arts in Communications from Harvard before beginning your career at WXBJ-FM. I also graduated from Harvard with a BA in English in May 2008 and since graduating, I have interned as a copy editor with Polygon. Over the past two years, I have also written content for social media, as well as working with the CEO in developing an offline marketing campaign. Although I enjoyed my role, I am interested in leveraging the strong organizational, communication and analytical skills that I've developed to obtain a position where I can have a more direct impact on an organization.
I would really appreciate it if we could set up a 20 to 30 minute meeting, at your convenience, to discuss any advice and suggestions that you might have as I further explore this industry. I look forward to hearing from you.
Sincerely,
Kristi Lenard

From: danielle_wilkinson@WXBJ.com
To: k.lenard@mail.com
Subject: RE: Request for Informational Interview – Harvard Alumni

Dear Ms. Lenard,
Thank you for reaching out to me. I would love to sit down to talk to you. Please let me know what time works for you next week.
Regards,
Danielle Wilkinson

From: k.lenard@mail.com
To: danielle_wilkinson@WXBJ.com
Subject: RE: RE: Request for Informational Interview – Harvard Alumni

Dear Ms. Wilkinson,
Thank you for getting back to me and willing to chat with me. Over the next week, I am free after 1p.m. on Monday and Tuesday afternoons as well as all day on Wednesday. Will any of those times work for you?
Thank you again,
Kristi

In the Business world, there will be many times when you need to write an e-mail. The reason for writing an e-mail will vary. However the format of an e-mail will stay the same.

An e-mail should always include:
  • Subject Line
  • Salutation
  • Body
  • Closing
  • Signature

Subject: Request for Informational Interview

Dear Mr. Smith,

I received your contact information from my mentor, Jane Doe, who said that you would be a great person to connect with in regards to ________________. I was hoping to gain some insight on ___________ and ________________.
I am a graduate of Boston University working/interested in ___________. Is there a possibility that we could connect for 15 minutes over the phone?

Thank you for your time and I look forward to hearing from you.

Regards,
Miley Moe

When you are writing an e-mail to a networking contact you may use gerunds.
Gerunds can be used as the subject, the complement or the object of your sentence. They can also be the object of the preposition in your sentence.
For example:
I am e-mailing you about setting up a meeting.
